newsitem.title: USA: Panamerican buys Venezuelan Coca-Cola bottler.
newsitem.headline: Panamerican buys Venezuelan Coca-Cola bottler.

text.p: Panamerican Beverages Inc said it has merged with Coca-Cola Hitt de Venezuela, a Coca-Cola bottler jointly owned by Coca-Cola Co and the Cisneros Group of Companies.
Under the terms of the transaction, it exchanged 30.6 million of its shares and about US$100.3 million in cash for all of Coca-Cola Hitt's stock, Panamco said in a statement.

The deal raises Coca Cola's stake in Panamco to about 25 percent, which includes 22.6 percent of the Venezuelan company's class A common shares and 25 percent of its class voting shares. The U.S. beverage giant previously held 13 percent of the class A shares and 16.0 percent of the class B shares.

The Cisneros Group, which combined its soft drink bottling interests in Venezuela in August with Coca Cola to form Coca-Cola y Hit, holds a 10.3 percent stake in each of Panamco's class A and class B voting shares, making them one of the largest of the company's shareholders, it said.
As part of the deal, Oswaldo Cisneros, chairman of Coca-Cola y Hit, and Gustavo Cisneros, chairman and chief executive officer of the Venezuela-based group, will join the Panamco board.

Mexico City-based Panamco, the largest soft drink bottler in Latin America and a large Coca-Cola "anchor" bottler with operations in Mexico, Brazil, Colombia and Costa Rica, will oversee day-to-day management of the Coca-Cola franchise in Venezuela, according to the statement.

Coca-Cola y Hit has an annual unit case volume of over 200 million and a customer base of about 23 million, Panmco said. With its Venezuela acquisition, its market base increases to 100 million consumers in Latin America, with projected sales of over one billion unit cases annually, Panamco said.

"Entering Venezuela reaffirms Panamco's leadership position as Latin Ameridca's largest soft drink bottler and will help us continue to deliver growth for our shareholders," said Francisco Sanchez-Loaeza, chairman and chief executive of Panamco.

M. Douglas Ivester, president and chief operating officer of Coca-Cola, said Panamco has become the second largest Coca-Cola bottler in the world and a key participant in the Coca-Cola's consolidation of its global bottling network.
